preconditions.description: T is an integer representing the number of test cases, where 1 ≤ T ≤ 150000.

preconditions.expression: all(n.is_integer() and 2 <= n <= 300000 for n in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()])
preconditions.description: Each test case starts with an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 300000) representing the number of monsters in the circle.

preconditions.expression: all(len(lines) == n + 1 for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly n lines following the n line, each containing two integers a_i and b_i (1 ≤ a_i, b_i ≤ 10^12).

preconditions.expression: all(all(a_i.is_integer() and b_i.is_integer() and 1 <= a_i <= 10**12 and 1 <= b_i <= 10**12 for a_i, b_i in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in lines[1:]]) for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: For each monster i, a_i and b_i are integers where 1 ≤ a_i, b_i ≤ 10^12.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line.is_integer() and output_line >= 0 for output_line in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of bullets required to kill all monsters.
The number of output lines equals the number of test cases T.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i] == min_bullets(n, a, b) for i, (n, a, b) in enumerate(zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[j:j+n] for j in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)] for line in lines], [tuple(map(int, line.split()))[1] for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[j:j+n] for j in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)] for line in lines])))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is the minimum number of bullets required to kill all monsters, where the function min_bullets(n, a, b) computes the minimum bullets needed to kill all monsters in a circle with n monsters, each having health a_i and explosion damage b_i. The function must account for the chain reaction of explosions when a monster dies.
